prompt: How has Falcon (FALC) been doing on velocity and say/do over its recent sprints? I'm trying to decide how much to commit for next sprint.
final_text:
Falcon finishes about **32 story points per sprint**, but the range is wide: 21 to 40. On average it completes **79% of what it commits to**. For next sprint I'd commit **about 30 points (roughly 10 items)**.

These figures cover Falcon's last 6 standard sprints (2026.18 to 2026.24). Sprint 2026.23 IP is left out because it was an innovation and planning sprint, which isn't comparable.

| Measure | Average | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Velocity (story points) | 31.8 | 21 to 40 |
| Velocity (items) | 10.5 | 8 to 13 |
| Predictability (points) | 88% | 65% to 100% |
| Say/do (points) | 79% | 57% to 94% |

**Sprint by sprint, most recent first:**
- 2026.24: 34 pts, 85% say/do
- 2026.22: 27 pts, 66% say/do
- 2026.21: 38 pts, 92% say/do
- 2026.20: 21 pts, 57% say/do. This was the weak one.
- 2026.19: 31 pts, 80% say/do
- 2026.18: 40 pts, 94% say/do

**What this means for planning:**
- Predictability (88%) is higher than say/do (79%). Predictability counts any finished work, including work added mid-sprint, while say/do counts only the work committed at the start. So Falcon often finishes added work in place of some of what it committed to. Leaving room for that work matters as much as the total you commit.
- I estimated how much Falcon committed each sprint by dividing velocity by predictability; Wayd doesn't report this directly. It comes out at roughly 32 to 40 points, about 35 most sprints. That's slightly more than Falcon finishes, which explains why say/do sits below 80%.
- **About 30 points** is just under the team's average velocity. It should push say/do toward the 85 to 90% the team reached in its good sprints.
- Use 34 to 36 points only if the sprint is unusually free of interruptions and the team is at full strength. Avoid going near 40: Falcon reached it once, and it's the top of the range.
- The most recent sprint (34 pts, 85%) was solid, but the team has swung between strong and weak sprints. One good sprint isn't enough reason to raise the commitment.

**Worth a look:** WIP load grades Healthy at 1 active item per member, but all 6 in-progress items are assigned to Marcus Hale. For a 6-person team, that's a concentration risk rather than an even spread.

**Bottom line:** the backlog isn't short of work, but you can't reliably estimate how long it will last yet.
